Subject: BrightPath MSA - redlines: provisional relief & choice of law

Hi Camila and Mark,

Attached are our MSAs redlines (see attachment: BrightPath_MSA_redlines_20270514.docx). Two key items the legal team flagged that we need your help on:

1) Provisional/equitable relief: BrightPath needs an explicit carve allowing our courts (US or EU as applicable) to grant injunctive or other provisional relief to preserve patient-safety related data and to enjoin imminent data processing that would violate EU law. We understand Redwood prefers arbitration clauses, but we need urgent-access to court relief in certain scenarios.

2) Governing law split for EU subsidiary: For European operations (BrightPath EU Ltd., a Luxembourg-registered subsidiary), we must have local governing law for matters related to data processing and regulatory compliance. BrightPath requests that the MSA allow the EU subsidiary to elect Luxembourg law and local courts for disputes concerning EU data/privacy/regulatory obligations.

We are happy to limit the provisional relief carve to narrow, urgent relief only (interim injunctions, preservation of evidence, or emergency suspension of a processing activity) but we cannot accept a clause that forces us into arbitration for those remedies.

Can Redwood legal propose specific language that: (a) preserves the right to seek provisional relief in courts; (b) allows the EU entity to elect local law/court for EU-regulatory matters; and (c) otherwise keeps the main dispute resolution mechanism (arbitration) intact for contract-level commercial disputes?

Please loop in counsel and suggest a path forward. We are on a tight procurement timeline — procurement would like a signed Order Form the week of May 24 if possible.

Thanks,
Sara Mensah

Camila / Laura — below are three drafting alternatives and a recommended approach. I kept the language tight so it can be inserted as a short carveout section in the MSA redline:

Option A (Customer-favored, broad):
"Notwithstanding the arbitration provisions in Section X, either party may seek injunctive or other provisional relief in any court of competent jurisdiction to prevent irreparable harm or preserve the status quo, including in relation to data protection or patient-safety matters. The foregoing shall not be deemed a waiver of the parties' agreement to arbitrate other disputes under this Agreement."

Risk: Very customer-friendly; increases litigation risk and forum shopping.

Option B (Recommended compromise):
"Notwithstanding the arbitration provisions in Section X, either party may seek interim injunctive or other provisional relief in a court of competent jurisdiction where necessary to prevent immediate and irreparable harm, to preserve evidence, or to address imminent risks to patient safety or data subject rights. Any such request for provisional relief shall be limited to the minimum relief necessary and shall in all events be without prejudice to the obligation of the parties to submit the underlying dispute to arbitration once the provisional relief has been granted or denied. For disputes arising out of or relating to the processing of personal data or regulatory compliance by BrightPath EU Ltd., BrightPath EU Ltd. may elect that Luxembourg law governs and that proceedings concerning such regulatory matters be brought in the courts of Luxembourg."
Risk note: Keeps arbitration as primary remedy, narrowly preserves court access for urgent relief, and permits a split governing-law election limited to regulatory/data matters for the EU entity. This limits exposure while meeting the customer's compliance requirement. We should add an express proviso that any injunctive relief sought must include notice to Redwood and, where practicable, an attempt to seek expedited arbitration remedies first.

Option C (Redwood-favored):
"The parties agree that all disputes arising under this Agreement shall be resolved exclusively by binding arbitration, and neither party may seek provisional remedies in court except with the prior written consent of the other party or where local law requires otherwise."

Risk: Unlikely to be acceptable to BrightPath's GC for EU/data/regulatory scenarios.

Suggested drafting changes and playbook:
- Use Option B as the working language. Add two short bullet points to the procurement pack: (1) Explanation that provisional relief is limited to urgent, narrowly tailored remedies; (2) Clarify that the Luxembourg election applies only to matters tied to BrightPath EU Ltd.'s regulatory obligations and does not alter contract-wide governing law for commercial claims.
- For jurisdiction venue: recommend naming "courts of Luxembourg" for EU-electable matters and "courts of San Francisco County, California" for US provisional relief (Redwood will accept local US courts for interim relief).
- Operational ask: If customer agrees to Option B, procurement team should add a sentence in the Order Form referencing the MSA carve (so downstream sys and finance see the exception).

Let me know if you want me to drop the exact redline into the Word doc and circulate back to BrightPath. If Sales approves, I'll prepare the redline and a two-paragraph exec note for the procurement team.

-Karthik
